newsitem.title: USA: Chubb sells real estate assets for $758 million.
newsitem.headline: Chubb sells real estate assets for $758 million.

text.p: Chubb Corp. said on Thursday it agreed to sell a substantial portion of its Bellemead Development Corp.'s commercial real estate properties to PW/MS Acquisition I LLC for $758 million.
The purchase price includes $649 million in cash and the assumption of $109 million in debt. Chubb said it expects to use the proceeds to pay down debt.
PW/MS Acquisition I is a joint venture company formed by Paine Webber Real Estate Securities Inc. and Morgan Stanley Real Estate Fund II LP.
Chubb, a big property-casualty insurer based in Warren, N.J., said the transaction is expected to close in the fall of 1997.
Chubb earlier this year sold its life insurance business to Jefferson-Pilot Corp. for $875 million in cash.
"With this sale, Chubb has taken a major step in its planned divestiture of real estate properties," said Chubb Chief Executive Dean O'Hare.
"We are receiving excellent value for these commercial properties and strengthening our balance sheet with their divestiture," he added.
He said Chubb also is proceeding with its previously announced plans to dispose of its residential and commercial real estate properties.
"These plans are on schedule," O'Hare said.

PW/MS Acquisition has agreed to buy interests in seven million square feet of suburban and metropolitan office properties and a portfolio of mortgage loans, PaineWebber Real Estate and Morgan Stanley Real Estate said.
The real estate portfolio to be acquired consists primarily of interests in 44 suburban office properties, largely concentrated in New Jersey, but also located in Michigan, Illinois and Maryland.

It also includes two high-rise metropolitan office properties: Fountain Place, an I.M. Pei-designed, 1.2 million-square-foot office building in downtown Dallas, and Franklin Court, a 443,000-square-food office property in the Franklin Square are of Washington, D.C.
